items.ab: To overcome the excessive sulfate (SO42-) production from single sulfur autotrophic denitrification (SAD) and the inability to achieve simultaneous phosphorus removal, this study constructed a synergistic sulfur‑iron autotrophic denitrification (SIAD) system mediated by S⁰ and Fe⁰. The effects of static magnetic field (MF) (15 mT) and inoculated sludge type (activated sludge, iron sludge) on nitrogen and phosphorus removal performance and microbial metabolism were investigated. MF accelerated Fe⁰ corrosion and Fe2+/Fe3+ release, enhancing chemical phosphorus precipitation in the SIAD system. The nitrogen removal contribution of SAD within the SIAD system is dynamically modulated by hydraulic retention time (HRT), with the effluent pH maintained at 8.3-8.5. items.t: OrthoDB and BUSCO update: broader phylogenomic sampling, deeper homology searches, and AI-agent support.
items.ab: OrthoDB (https://www.orthodb.org) provides evolutionary and functional annotations of orthologous genes across the broadest range of organismal diversity. It extends experimentally acquired knowledge from well-studied organisms to newly sequenced genomes, delineating orthologous groups (OGs) hierarchically at explicit taxonomic levels and annotating them with collated functional evidence and evolutionary traits. This release updates eukaryotic coverage to 5768 genomes, including 132 mammalian genomes re-annotated with Tiberius, and incorporates an updated selection of the latest available fungal and protist genomes. The OGs were recomputed de novo with OrthoLoger from MMseqs2 candidate homology searches using optimized parameters. To better recover remote homology at the Eukaryota root and among divergent protist sequences, we used the The Embedded Alphabet (TEA) protein-language-model-derived alphabet. This increased OG assignment, with greater representation of least diverged orthologs. BUSCO lineage datasets were rebuilt for eukaryotes using broader and more evenly represented species sampling, further extending their value for metagenome-assembled genomes and microbial eukaryotes. The OrthoDB web interface now includes a source-linked conversational assistant, and a Model Context Protocol layer exposes public API endpoints to external AI agents. items.t: Transcriptional markers of organic substrate utilization in a marine bacterium.
items.ab: Marine dissolved organic carbon is a chemically complex substrate pool that fuels heterotrophic bacteria, yet it remains difficult to determine which compounds are used by specific microbes. Bacterial transcriptomes offer a potential biosensor of substrate availability, but the reliability of this approach in chemically mixed substrates remains uncertain. Here, we evaluated the reliability of this transcriptional sensor approach using the model marine bacterium Ruegeria pomeroyi DSS-3 grown on either glucose or a defined mixture containing glycerol, benzoate, succinate, leucine, dimethylsulfoniopropionate, and trimethylamine N-oxide. Genome-wide transcription differed strongly between treatments, with the mixed-substrate treatment enriched in genes associated with C1 metabolism, sulfur oxidation, benzoate degradation, and motility. Under the conditions tested, the clearest treatment-associated transcriptional differences occurred at pathway entry points and first committed reactions, including glucose transport and Entner-Doudoroff metabolism, trimethylamine N-oxide transport and catabolism, and early steps of aerobic benzoate oxidation. In contrast, downstream metabolic genes were less substrate-specific, likely because multiple pathways converged on shared central metabolic intermediates. items.ab: Partial denitrification-anammox saves organic carbon in mainstream nitrogen removal, but most systems rely on dosed organic or sulfur donors and few were pilot-tested. A 270-L pilot comprising anaerobic pretreatment, oxygen-limited nitrification and a sulfide-driven partial denitrification-anammox (SDA) reactor was operated on real municipal wastewater for 432 days without external electron donors, first in series, then with half of the anaerobic effluent bypassing nitrification (split feed). Nitrification at 0.46-0.61 mg O2/L remained nitrate-dominated, with incomplete suppression of nitrite-oxidising bacteria. Under series feed, ammonium passed the SDA reactor almost unchanged while regenerated nitrite was denitrified heterotrophically. Split feed raised the ammonium entering the SDA reactor from 18.8 to 33.1 mg-N/L, its ammonium removal from 0.4 to 14.1 mg-N/L and nitrogen removal rate from 68.5 to 93.4 g-N/m3/d. Nitrogen balances attributed at most 46% of this ammonium removal to anammox, with aerobic oxidation at low dissolved oxygen also contributing. items.t: Haloalkalitolerant Billgrantia alkalidenitrificans sp. nov. isolated from cathodic biofilm enriched with Soda Lake sediments and genomic insights into the key metabolic functionality of the Billgranti
items.ab: Extreme environments host diverse but underexplored microbial communities. Many microbes remain uncultured due to the limitations of existing isolation techniques. This study reports a novel haloalkalitolerant nitrate-reducing, Gram-negative bacterium, Billgrantia alkalidenitrificans NRB1, isolated from the cathodic biofilm enriched electrochemically using sub-surface sediments from Lonar Lake (Soda Lake, India), and presents a genome-based analysis of the major metabolic functions of the genus Billgrantia, recently reclassified from the genus Halomonas. Physiological experiments demonstrated that NRB1 is a facultative anaerobe that displays remarkable adaptability to a wide range of salinities (0-150 g NaCl/L; optimum 20-50 g NaCl/L), temperatures (10°C-45°C; optimum 37°C), and pH (6.5-11.5; optimum 9.5). It is capable of utilizing several sugars, sulfide oxidation, and respiration on oxygen, nitrate (via denitrification), and nitrite. These experimental observations were consistent with genome analysis, which predicted a complete set of genes for denitrification, sulfide oxidation, and sugar metabolism pathways, also detected in other Billgrantia species. Genome analysis further predicted the presence of arsenic resistance and ectoine-synthesizing genes in NRB1. Phylogenetic analysis using the 16S rRNA gene, orthologous genes, and whole-genome sequencing revealed that strain NRB1 clustered closely with Billgrantia campisalis 4A, the closest reference taxon. items.t: Antimicrobial activity of extremophilic bacteria and archaea: screening of enrichments, binary associations and culture collections.
items.ab: During the "golden age" of antibiotics research (1940s-1970s) soil microbial communities, and especially actinomycetes of the genus Streptomyces, were the main source of novel molecules with antimicrobial activity. However, after 1980 it has become challenging to find new classes of antibiotics from familiar sources. At the same time, microbial resistance to existing antibiotic drugs showed the capacity to spread rapidly among bacteria, especially those of clinical importance. Thus, new groups of bacteria and new environments became a promising source of the new molecules with antimicrobial activity. In this work we performed screening of extremophilic enrichments and culture collections of Winogradsky Institute of Microbiology, Research Center of Biotechnology RAS, for the presence of microorganisms producing antimicrobial compounds. The screening revealed antimicrobial activities of thermophilic bacteria of Bacillus and Anoxybacillus genera, as well as alkaliphilic Streptomyces isolates against Gram-positive and Gram-negative pathogenic bacteria including clinically important and resistant strains. It was also found that hyperthermophilic strain of the genus Thermococcus and several co-cultures of other archaea belonging to the order Thermoproteales produce compounds suppressing the growth of Gram-positive and Gram-negative pathogens. items.t: Machine learning prediction of antimicrobial resistance in respiratory metagenomes
items.ab: Background Targeted therapy for patients with suspected respiratory infections traditionally requires bacterial culture followed by phenotypic antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST), a process that can take up to 5 days. In acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), delays in identifying the causative pathogen and its resistance profile may be especially harmful because patients are critically ill and often receive broad-spectrum empiric antibiotics. The growing burden of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) further complicates clinical decision-making by reducing effective treatment options and increasing the risk of inadequate initial therapy. Culture-free, AI-driven computational metagenomic strategies have the potential to drastically shorten this window, enabling more rapid targeted therapy prescription. To show the feasibility of such approaches, we develop a proof-of-concept framework based on clinical metagenomics. Methods We simulated respiratory metagenomes using real-world bacterial genomes with associated antimicrobial susceptibility phenotypes. Each simulated metagenome contained a fixed commensal background and one clinically important respiratory pathogen, Acinetobacter baumannii , Klebsiella pneumoniae , or Pseudomonas aeruginosa , at 5% or 10% bacterial read abundance. items.t: Chemolithoautotrophic acidophile phenotyping by measuring metabolic byproduct formation in microplates
items.ab: Chemolithoautotrophic acidophiles can support several low-pH biotechnologies, but their phenotyping remains limited by throughput and inconsistent methods. This study used an assay to monitor metabolic byproduct formation using absorbance indicators in static, oxic cultures in 96-well microplates. In abiotic experiments, ferric iron and/or pH measurements from 51 microplates containing simulant solutions span total iron concentrations of 0–1 M, pH 0.3–7.0, and incubation temperatures of 4–75 ◦C. Of these, 30 microplates tested different UV-transparency and gas-permeable membrane configurations. Another 12 microplates tested indicator compatibility with growth media containing ferrous iron and (in)soluble sulfur substrates. Biological experiments measured 438 microplates containing Acidithiobacillus ferrooxidans ATCC 23270, Acidithiobacillus thiooxidans ATCC 19377, or Leptospirillum ferriphilum DSM 14647 with chemical additives across 1,400 concentration conditions, yielding 142,038 time-course points, including abiotic controls. Measurements of apparent substrate oxidation and/or growth from 96 culture tubes and 99 shake flasks provide context for microplate observations. The miniaturized assay and this dataset may be useful for microbiology, (critical-mineral) biotechnology development, and synthetic biology.

items.t: Carbon monoxide utilization by Thermanaeromonas species and description of Thermobium azorense gen. nov., sp. nov.
items.ab: Syngas fermentation by carbon monoxide (CO)-utilizing acetogens offers a sustainable route for converting gasified waste materials into value-added chemicals. In this study, we isolated a novel thermophilic CO-utilizing bacterium, strain AZ2, from marine hydrothermal sediment collected on the island of São Miguel, Azores, Portugal. Strain AZ2 is an obligately anaerobic, spore-forming bacterium. Average nucleotide identity (ANI) and digital DNA-DNA hybridization (dDDH) analyses indicate that strain AZ2 represents a novel species within a previously uncharacterized lineage represented by the GTDB placeholder genus UBA 12545 in Neomoorellaceae. It is also the first cultured representative of this genus. Strain AZ2 was able to consume CO, producing acetate. We further demonstrated that its closest isolated relatives-Thermanaeromonas toyohensis and Thermanaeromonas sp. strain 9S-are capable of utilizing CO, producing either acetate or hydrogen gas (H2). Additionally, we unveiled the genomic potential for CO utilization within other members of the GTDB placeholder class DSM-521 (previously Moorellia) to which our isolate belongs, expanding the list of possible thermophilic CO-utilizing acetogens. We propose that strain AZ2T represents the type strain of a novel genus and species, named Thermobium azorense gen. nov., sp. nov. (= DSM 121889T = JCM 39698T).

items.t: Culture-benchmarked metagenomics maps microbial strain sharing in long-term acute care.
items.ab: Long-term acute care hospitals (LTACHs) are major reservoirs for multidrug-resistant organisms (MDROs), yet conventional surveillance methods based on culture and targeted sequencing incompletely characterize microbial transmission. Metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) offers the potential to capture strain-level transmission dynamics across the broader microbiome, providing a more comprehensive view of healthcare-associated microbial spread. We conducted a prospective observational cohort study of 49 LTACH patients from April to July 2023. All LTACH patients provided perirectal samples on Weeks 1 and 6; a subset of patients who received fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) submitted enhanced weekly sampling for a six-week period at the time of and after FMT administration. Samples underwent mNGS and were selectively cultured for MRDOs, with cultured isolates undergoing whole genome sequencing (WGS). We developed an open-source computational pipeline, MAG-based Strain Profiling and Identification (MAGSPI), which reconstructs metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs), collapses them into species-level genome bins (SGBs), and enables strain-level comparisons using inStrain. WGS-defined strain assignments served as the reference standard for optimization of strain-sharing thresholds. items.t: Bioleaching assisted multiple metal recovery from printed circuit boards
items.ab: Abstract Electronic waste (e-waste) generation is increasing rapidly, highlighting the need for sustainable recovery of valuable metals. Printed circuit boards (PCBs) are particularly rich in both precious and hazardous metals, necessitating efficient extraction methods. In this study, we present a two-step bioleaching and chemical precipitation approach to recover multiple metals from alkali-pretreated mobile phone PCBs using an acidophilic bacterial strain isolated from sewage sludge. The strain was acclimated over six successive cycles to highly acidic conditions, demonstrated by pH reduction of the medium to pH 1, and Fe 2+ oxidation to Fe 3+ . Subsequent bioleaching achieved significant metal solubilisation from the PCBs: Ni 99.32 ± 0.09% > Cu 69.73 ± 0.43% > Al 33.88 ± 0.01% > Zn 27.56 ± 0.01% >Pb 3.27 ± 0.01 %. The resulting acidic bioleachate was neutralised with NaOH, precipitating metals non-selectively with an overall recovery efficiency exceeding 94%. This approach offers a sustainable and environmentally benign route for multi-metal recovery from e-waste, supporting circular economy and resource management initiatives.

items.t: Evaluation of Water Quality of the Benso Reclaimated Acid Mine Drainage Site in the Mpohor District
items.ab: Abstract Extraction industry in Ghana is one of the most economically viable industry fetching huge returns to the country. items.t: Draft genome sequences of green-pigmented Pseudoalteromonas luteoviolacea GB1 and Pseudoalteromonas rubra GB2 isolated from seawater of Chuuk lagoon
items.ab: Abstract Objectives Pigmented Pseudoalteromonas strains are renowned for producing diverse bioactive secondary metabolites, yet genome-level characterization of green-pigmented strains—an unusual phenotype within species canonically exhibiting red or purple pigmentation—has not been reported. Here, we describe the draft genome sequences of two green-pigmented marine isolates, Pseudoalteromonas luteoviolacea GB1 and Pseudoalteromonas rubra GB2, both of which exhibited antimicrobial activity against bacteria and fungi, including Candida spp. Data description Both genomes were sequenced using the PacBio long-read platform. P. luteoviolacea GB1 was assembled into 37 contigs (6.06 Mb; N50 308,453 bp; 99.47% complete) and P. rubra GB2 into 4 contigs (5.84 Mb; N50 4,456,163 bp; 93.59% complete). Genome annotation, phylogenomic placement, and biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC) prediction were performed. Both strains were confirmed as members of their respective named species. BGC prediction identified clusters highly similar to the canonical violacein (GB1) and prodigiosin (GB2) biosynthetic pathways, despite the atypical green pigmentation in both strains. Multiple additional BGCs with predicted antimicrobial functions were identified. These datasets provide a resource for investigating the genomic basis of an unusual pigmentation phenotype and for mining novel bioactive compounds from marine Pseudoalteromonas .

items.t: Integrating machine learning and molecular docking analysis reveals the molecular network associated with tris(1,3-dichloro-2-propyl) phosphate in hepatocellular carcinoma
items.ab: Abstract Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is one of the most common primary liver malignancies worldwide and represents a major global health burden. Increasing evidence suggests that environmental pollutants may contribute to hepatocarcinogenesis. Tris(1,3-dichloro-2-propyl) phosphate (TDCPP) is a widely used organophosphate flame retardant. Current studies have clearly demonstrated that TDCPP possesses genotoxicity, hepatotoxicity, and carcinogenic potential. However, the molecular mechanisms linking TDCPP exposure to HCC remain unclear. The aim of this study was to explore the potential toxic targets and molecular mechanisms of TDCPP-associated HCC using an integrative bioinformatics approach. Transcriptomic datasets were obtained from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database. Differential expression analysis and weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) were performed to identify HCC-related genes, while TDCPP targets were predicted using ChEMBL, SwissTargetPrediction, and PharmMapper. Intersection analysis, functional enrichment analysis, machine learning, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), and molecular docking were subsequently conducted. The results identified 230 potential TDCPP-related HCC targets. Enrichment analyses indicated involvement in pathways associated with cell cycle regulation, DNA replication, p53 signaling, FoxO signaling, and cellular senescence. items.t: Genome-resolved multi-omics reveals microbiome reorganization and carbon-flow regulation driven by functional bioaugmentation in thermophilic anaerobic digestion.
items.ab: Bioaugmentation has emerged as a promising strategy for manipulating complex microbial ecosystems. However, the ecological mechanisms determining whether introduced microorganisms can functionally integrate into indigenous communities remain poorly understood. Here, genome-resolved metagenomics and metabolomics were combined to investigate how B. thermoamylovorans Y25 influenced microbial succession and ecosystem-level carbon transformation. Y25 successfully established within the thermophilic anaerobic microbiome and promoted a 12.69% (472.00 ± 27.69 NmL g-1 VS, p < 0.05) increase in cumulative methane yield without compromising reactor stability. This improvement occurred without significant changes in methanogenesis-related genes. Instead, Y25 bioaugmentation induced pronounced shifts in microorganisms associated with hydrolysis and fermentation and enhanced pathways related to substrate transport and intermediate carbon metabolism, accompanied by coordinated metabolite changes. These findings support a transition from strain-centered bioaugmentation strategies toward an ecosystem-level perspective, highlighting that successful microbial engineering depends on ecological integration and functional coordination within indigenous microbial networks.

items.t: One Health phylogenomics of antibiotic-resistant Salmonella enterica reveals cross-source relatedness and detection of mcr-3-carrying ST34 isolates in Hong Kong.
items.ab: Nontyphoidal Salmonella enterica serovars are a major driver of foodborne illnesses in Hong Kong. Beyond well-recognized extended spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL)- and carbapenemase-producing strains, colistin resistance remains a critical concern for treating severe multidrug-resistant (MDR) infections. While routine surveillance exists, the distribution and genomic epidemiology of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) across interconnected reservoirs remain insufficiently characterized. Applying a One Health framework, this study investigated cross-sectoral genetic relatedness and shared AMR determinants by analysing local clinical and retail meat Salmonella isolates alongside a reference set of publicly available regional genomes representing human, food, animal, and environmental sectors. We report the detection of mcr-positive S. Typhimurium ST34 lineage human clinical isolates in Hong Kong, including mcr-1.1 and mcr-3.1, not previously detected in our regional dataset or local genomic surveillance archives. Nanopore sequencing revealed that mcr-3 was carried on a mosaic IncC/IncFII plasmid displaying structural features consistent with a recombinant origin involving genetic elements shared between clinical Salmonella and chicken-derived E. coli plasmid backbones. items.t: hlafactor: a tool for multi-layer functional annotation of HLA variation.
items.ab: MOTIVATION: The human leukocyte antigen (HLA) system is the most polymorphic region of the human genome and a major determinant of immune function and disease susceptibility. Ideally, analyses of HLA variation would capture multiple layers of information, from classical alleles and amino-acid residues to higher-level functional properties such as tapasin dependency, cell-surface expression, and NK cell ligand groups. However, while allele- and amino-acid-level data are now routinely available, the corresponding functional annotations remain scattered across publications and reference datasets, and no existing tool integrates them within a unified, reproducible framework. RESULTS: We present hlafactor, a computational tool that brings together established HLA functional annotations within a single, standardised framework. Starting from two-field HLA genotype calls, whether imputed or molecularly typed, hlafactor assigns functional annotations from published reference datasets and applies established calculations to derive individual-level features. These include tapasin dependency scores, general and functional heterozygosity, allele-specific cell surface expression, NK cell-related polymorphisms (Bw4/Bw6, C1/C2, HLA-B -21 M/T), and class I/II supertype assignments. hlafactor also maps alleles to IMGT/HLA amino-acid alignments to generate residue-level genotypes. items.t: Gut Microbiome Networks Across Schizophrenia, Major Depressive Disorder, and Bipolar Disorder: A Systematic Reanalysis and Machine Learning Study
items.ab: Psychiatric disorders represent a leading cause of global disease burden, yet their accurate and timely diagnosis remains challenging due to incomplete understanding of etiology and a lack of objective pathognomonic features. These factors leave diagnosis and treatment vulnerable to diagnostic errors. This diagnostic uncertainty, alongside emerging evidence linking the microbiota-gut-brain axis to psychiatric pathophysiology, has fueled the ongoing search for objective microbial biomarkers. We systematically searched PubMed and Scopus for gut microbiome 16S sequencing studies involving patients with schizophrenia (SCZ), major depressive disorder (MDD), and bipolar disorder (BD) that had publicly available sequencing read data. Data were extracted and analyzed through a harmonized bioinformatics pipeline to assess differences in α- and β-diversity and microbial composition. Co-occurrence networks were constructed, and differences in network topology, hubs, and taxon centrality were investigated. Finally, a random forest (RF) and a convolutional neural network ensemble (CNN) classifier were trained, and their performance in predicting diagnosis from microbiome composition was evaluated using two different cross-validation schemes. items.t: Reconstructing Occluded Joints in 3D Human Pose Sequences: A Real-Occlusion Benchmark and an Interpolation-Initialised Spatio-Temporal Transformer.
items.ab: Three-dimensional (3D) pose estimators lose joints whenever a limb is hidden, yet learned reconstruction of missing joints is usually developed with simulated occlusion, because the true positions of occluded joints are rarely known. This study evaluates reconstruction under real occlusion with measured ground truth: in 3D Poses in the Wild (3DPW), a joint is lost when its OpenPose confidence falls below 0.3, while body-worn inertial sensors give its true position; CMU Panoptic, Human3.6M, and MPI-INF-3DHP serve as zero-shot tests. The benchmark therefore scores the joints that a real detector misses in real video, which is what a deployed system has to fill, rather than joints annotated as physically occluded. Thirteen models were compared with five seeds and a paired video-level bootstrap, including the proposed Occlusion-Aware Skeleton Spatiotemporal Transformer (OA-Skeleton ST), which starts from linear interpolation and learns a visibility-aware residual correction, and which is pretrained on AMASS motion capture with simulated masks before fine-tuning on 3DPW. On the joints really lost in 24 test videos, OA-Skeleton ST reached the lowest mean per-joint position error, at 79.1 mm: 13.7 mm below interpolation with a kinematic fallback (95% CI 9.0-17.6 mm, better on 87.5% of videos) and 6.7 mm below a plain spatiotemporal transformer (95% CI 4.9-8.7 mm, better on every video). items.t: De novo Genome Assembly and Annotation of the Seep Tubeworm Lamellibrachia satsuma using Oxford Nanopore Sequencing
items.ab: The tubeworm Lamelllibrachia satsuma inhabits seep region by forming a mutualistic symbiotic relationship with chemosynthetic bacteria residing in its trophosome. Genomic and symbiotic studies have been extensively conducted, primarily from a bacterial perspective. But rarely vice versa. Here we present a high-quality draft genome assembly of L. satsuma and its tissue-specific transcriptome data. This genome will be valuable for further understanding the mechanisms of adaptation in cold seep environments, host-microbe interactions, as well as genome variation among tubeworms. We generated ~103 Gb of genomic sequencing data using Illumina and Oxford Nanopore platforms, which assembled in a 665 Mb draft genome. The assembled genome consisted of 6,320 scaffolds with 95.7% genome completeness. Among 32,394 predicted protein-coding genes, 1,063 gene families have expanded, and 1,385 gene families were contracted. Among the expanded gene families, multiple copies of leukocyte elastase inhibitor, reverse transcriptase, arylesterase, and xanthine dehydrogenase/oxidase genes were found. Molecular clock analysis based on the phylogenomic dataset revealed that L. sastuma and L. luymesi were diverged from their common ancestor during the Early Cenozoic era, approximately 13 million years ago.

items.t: Benchmarking Machine Learning Methods for Antimicrobial Peptide Prediction and Discovery in Ancient Microbiomes
items.ab: Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) offer a promising alternative to conventional antibiotics amid the growing global threat of antimicrobial resistance. Expanding AMP discovery requires both effective computational tools to accurately identify candidate peptides and access to underexplored biological resources that may harbor novel AMPs. However, the comparative performance of existing computational methods remains poorly understood, while ancient microbiomes have received limited attention as potential reservoirs of AMPs. Here, we systematically benchmarked six machine learning methods across with twelve feature configurations spanning sequence, structural, and protein language model features under a unified framework using eight curated AMP datasets. The best-performing methods were subsequently applied to three ancient metagenomic datasets representing the human gut (archaeological fecal sediments), human oral cavity (dental calculus), and mammoth-associated communities (teeth, skulls, and skin). In parallel, we employed reinforcement learning to select candidate peptides directly from ancient sequence pools without relying on modern AMP labels. Our benchmarking shows that protein language model embeddings provide the most informative features, and deep learning models, including convolutional, transformer-based, and recurrent architectures, outperform classical methods. items.ab: ABSTRACT Filamentous anoxygenic phototrophs (FAPs) of the Chloroflexota phylum are abundant members of microbial mat communities. All isolated and culturable FAPs are found in a single class within this phylum, but metagenomic studies of hot spring communities from around the world have indicated that phototrophic members of an additional class may exist, which have so far eluded cultivation for study in the laboratory. items.t: Comparative metagenomics of extremophilic microbiomes from Pakistan reveals a conserved taxonomic core and habitat-specific functional gene signatures.
items.ab: Microbial communities inhabiting extreme environments serve as valuable models for understanding microbial diversity under environmental stress and represent potential reservoirs of novel functional diversity with biotechnological relevance. items.t: Know Thy Neighbour: Benchmarking Protein Language Model Embedding-Based Annotation Reveals Anisotropy Substantially Impacts Retrieval
items.ab: Functional annotation using protein language models (‘pLMs’) usually proceeds by transferring the function of a query’s nearest neighbour in a reference database. A major drawback is that embedding-based annotation transfer has no null model, i.e. no accepted way to set a cosine-similarity threshold to control false positives. This contrasts with traditional bioinformatics methods, including sequence- and structure-based alignment tools, which rank hits with E-values derived from explicit null models. Here, we benchmark final-layer, mean-pooled embeddings from twelve models against MMseqs2 and Foldseek for remote-homology retrieval on curated datasets based on Swiss-Prot and SCOPe, fixing per-model thresholds at a 1% false-positive rate and probing the score with a ladder of synthetic decoys. These two pLM families exhibit extreme anisotropy, using fewer than 15 effective dimensions out of 640–2560, and low effective dimensionality is strongly associated with poor performance across models. items.t: A specialized microbiome enriched in nitrification and halogen cycling potential resolved from multi-omics investigation of a Caribbean suboxic and acidic marine sinkhole.
items.ab: BACKGROUND: The Luymes Sinkholes, located on the Luymes Bank northwest of Saba, represent a unique marine environment characterized by distinct biogeochemical gradients. Most noticeable is an acidic (pH ≈ 6.25) and suboxic (O2 < 60 µmol/kg) submerged 'lake' at ~ 220 m depth exhibiting extreme deviations from standard oceanographic patterns, including elevated inorganic carbon, nitrate, and phosphate, and a lower temperature (20.3 ºC vs 26.4 ºC). RESULTS: We identified a distinct microbial community within the submerged acid lake different from the non-acidic sinkholes, with increased abundances of Nitrospinota, Thermoproteota, Planctomycetota, and Actinobacteriota. We also found three enriched classes of dissolved compounds within the submerged acid lake: (1) large, (2) low-polarity, and (3) halogenated metabolites, including iodides and halobenzoic acids. Correlations between microbial taxa and metabolite classes show potential links between nitrifying archaea and halogenated compound cycling. items.t: Genome assembly and functional annotation of capirona (Calycophyllum spruceanum): genomic insights into an Amazonian timber tree
items.ab: Abstract Calycophyllum spruceanum (Benth.) Hook.f. ex K.Schum. (Rubiaceae) is an Amazonian timber tree whose bark is used in traditional medicine, but genomic resources for the species are scarce. We report the first draft nuclear genome of the species, assembled from 323.8 million Illumina read pairs of a single tree (~ 185× coverage after trimming). k-mer analysis estimated a haploid genome size of 499–503 Mb and a heterozygosity of approximately 1%. After removal of organellar and microbial sequences, the final draft assembly spans 506.9 Mb in 72,381 scaffolds (N50 = 11.5 kb), with a GC content of 34.2%. It contains 83.9% of conserved single-copy eudicot genes (BUSCO) as complete copies; 19% of these genes are duplicated, consistent with retained allelic copies. Repeats cover 40.3% of the assembly, being mostly unclassified elements and LTR retrotransposons, with Gypsy elements about three times more abundant than Copia. We identified 266,057 simple sequence repeats (SSRs; 529.0 per Mb), a higher density than in Coffea canephora Pierre ex A.Froehner and Emmenopterys henryi Oliv., with AT-rich motifs predominating. Homology-based annotation from three Coffea genomes predicted 36,690 protein-coding genes, 97.1% of which received at least one homology-based functional annotation. This draft is the first nuclear reference for the genus Calycophyllum and a source of candidate SSR loci for the conservation and breeding of capirona genetic resources.

items.t: DynamicsPLM: A Dynamics-Enriched Small Protein Language Model for Protein Variant Effect Prediction
items.ab: ABSTRACT Predicting how mutations impact protein function and stability remains a key challenge in computational biology. Current state-of-the-art protein language models (PLMs) primarily scale parameter size on sequence corpora to capture evolutionary constraints but remain blind to the explicit physical dynamics of folded proteins. Conversely, models trained strictly on physical dynamics neglect critical evolutionary sequence statistics. In this paper, we bridge this gap by introducing DynamicsPLM, a highly parameter-efficient 35-million-parameter model that unifies evolutionary and biophysical representation learning. Utilizing a second-stage, multi-task continual pretraining strategy on over 60,000 proteins, we enrich a foundational sequence encoder with explicit residue-level and pairwise molecular dynamics heads while preserving its original evolutionary knowledge. At inference, DynamicsPLM computes zero-shot mutation effects from sequence alone by balancing an evolutionary plausibility score against a structural dynamics disruption score. Across the massive ProteinGym benchmark and natural variants of the Tsuboyama folding stability dataset, DynamicsPLM achieves state-of-the-art accuracy among all models under 100M parameters, and matches or outperforms several billion-scale sequence-based models of its size. items.ab: The biological remediation of complex petroleum waste streams suffers from severe performance bottlenecks in industrial and marine settings due to the simultaneous thermal, osmotic and mechanical stress. In these hypersaline and multi-extreme matrices, such as produced water, coastal oil spills, and refinery lagoons, conventional mesophiles succumb to rapid plasmolysis, catalytic deceleration, and metabolic uncoupling. items.t: From Phenotype to Phylogenomics: Evolution of Lactobacillaceae Taxonomy, the 2020 Reclassification and its Technological and Regulatory Implications.
items.ab: Lactic acid bacteria (LAB) are a diverse group of microorganisms with major importance in food fermentation, biopreservation, probiotic development, and biotechnology. Advances in molecular biology and whole-genome sequencing have revealed limitations of traditional phenotype-based classification, driving a transition toward genome-based taxonomy and fundamentally reshaping the classification of the family Lactobacillaceae. This review traces the evolution of LAB taxonomy from classical phenotypic classification through the molecular era to contemporary phylogenomic approaches. It examines the genomic methodologies underpinning modern bacterial systematics, including whole-genome sequencing, Average Nucleotide Identity (principally a species-level measure), Average Amino Acid Identity, and core-genome phylogenetics, which culminated in the landmark 2020 reclassification of the former genus Lactobacillus into 25 phylogenetically coherent genera. The review further evaluates the scientific evidence supporting this reclassification and its validation through subsequent phylogenomic, pangenomic, and ecological studies. Genome-based taxonomy has established a more evolutionarily coherent and biologically informative classification of Lactobacillaceae, improving our understanding of ecological adaptation, metabolic diversity, and functional potential. items.ab: Methanogenic archaea play crucial roles in sedimentary phosphorus cycling, but their capacity for phosphate biomineralization remains poorly understood. Here we demonstrate that Methanobacterium AMB_03, isolated from a serpentinizing environment, mediates extracellular precipitation of carbonate-substituted hydroxyapatite (HAp) under phosphate-enriched conditions. Phylogenomic analysis of 320 Methanobacteriota genomes further shows that complete polyP cycling capacity is present in only ∼25% of representatives, placing AMB_03 among a minority of methanogens with this capability. Experimental cultivation across phosphate gradients (0-6 mM) showed HAp early-onset precipitation was preferential at ≥3 mM. items.ab: Lactic acid bacteria (LAB) are a physiologically defined and taxonomically diverse group of Gram-positive fermentative organisms central to food production, probiotic development, and microbial biotechnology. Their continual exposure to bacteriophages and mobile DNA has selected multiple defense strategies, but the same defenses can make industrial and non-model isolates difficult to transform or edit genetically. Restriction-modification (R-M) systems are central to this conflict because they discriminate incoming DNA according to sequence and modification state, thereby influencing phage infection, plasmid transfer, transformation, and recombination. items.ab: Predicting protein melting temperature (Tm) and organismal optimal growth temperature (OGT) is essential for enzyme engineering, biocatalyst design, and metagenomic bioprospecting, yet computational prediction faces several fundamental bottlenecks: sequence-only representations miss tertiary packing; dual-task coupling induces destructive gradient conflict; natural database skew (>87% mesophiles) drives mesophilic collapse; and existing tools produce uncalibrated point predictions. items.ab: The seagrass rhizosphere microbiome is critical for sedimentary nutrient turnover, yet the spatiotemporal dynamics of carbon, nitrogen, phosphorus, and sulfur cycling across Zostera marina developmental stages remain poorly understood. Nitrogen fixation and dissimilatory nitrate reduction to ammonium (DNRA) genes were enriched in the rhizosphere during both vegetative and dormant stages. items.t: Phylogenomic coupling of F1 chemosensory and archaellum systems across archaea and monoderm bacteria.
items.ab: Archaellum-associated motility has been viewed as solely archaeal, yet new findings in Chloroflexota prompt a broader perspective. By analysing a curated ~22 000 NCBI reference genomes alongside 2397 archaeal and 226 archaellum-encoding Chloroflexota genomes, this study systematically characterizes the co-distribution of archaellum loci with chemosensory system (CSS) classes. Maximum-likelihood phylogeny of 3727 F1-type CheA proteins reveals three major clades, with Clade 1 comprising ~80% monoderm representation, uniting archaeal and monoderm bacterial lineages in a shared evolutionary grouping. Overall, this work shows that not only archaeal-type motility, but also F1-CSS-based sensing system might have been gained from Archaea to Chloroflexota via horizontal gene transfer, and both systems shared an evolutionary trajectory altogether.

items.t: Substantial genetic potential for deep-sea chemoautotrophy extends beyond nitrifiers.
items.ab: Microbial chemoautotrophy has the potential to sustain ecosystems at depth, contribute to global carbon sequestration, and ameliorate the currently unbalanced marine carbon budget. However, an understanding of its mechanisms is still emerging, particularly beyond organisms performing nitrification. Here, we conduct a combined gene-based and genome-resolved analysis of 28 metagenomes from the Northeast Pacific Ocean to investigate the prevalence, distribution, and phylogenetic and metabolic diversity of marine chemoautotrophs. We find that organisms encoding marker genes for autotrophic dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC) fixation are abundant and widespread within our samples, comprising 11%-26% of microbial communities from 150 to 4,000 m water depth. Marker genes for the Calvin cycle and 3-hydroxypropionate bi-cycles are more prevalent than those for the 3-hydroxypropionate/4-hydroxybutyrate and reverse tricarboxylic acid cycles, the latter two of which are encoded by organisms conducting nitrification. We constructed and identified 128 putatively chemoautotrophic metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs), spanning 13 phyla including the Proteobacteria, Actinobacteria, SAR324, and the Thermoproteota. These MAGs contain genes for the oxidation of carbon monoxide (77.3%), sulfur (69.5%), ammonia (5.5%), and/or methane (3.1%), suggesting that diverse catabolisms support deep-sea DIC fixation and an underappreciated potential role for aerobic carbon monoxide oxidation. items.ab: UNLABELLED: The genus Rickettsia comprises obligate intracellular bacteria belonging to the class Alphaproteobacteria. Although Rickettsia species have traditionally been classified into several phylogenetic groups, recent genome-based studies have revealed greater diversity within the genus and related Rickettsiaceae lineages than previously recognized. Here, we isolated six rickettsial strains from Ixodes turdus ticks collected at various locations across Japan and performed whole-genome sequencing. A closed-genome sequence was obtained for one of the isolates. R. mendelii" were smaller (1.05-1.06 Mb) and had lower GC content (29.2-29.3%) than most analyzed rickettsial genomes and were comparable in these respects to those of Typhus Group rickettsiae. Family-wide phylogenomic analysis using a quality-filtered Rickettsiaceae genome data set placed "Ca. R. mendelii" in a distinct early-diverging lineage within the genus Rickettsia. items.t: Associations of gut microbial and serum metabolic features with metabolic comorbidities in patients with NAFLD.
items.ab: INTRODUCTION: Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) coexists with dyslipidemia or impaired fasting glucose (IFG), but gut microbial and serum metabolic features remain incompletely characterized. Dialister invisus was administered to high-calorie diet-fed mice, and metabolic and hepatic outcomes were assessed. items.t: Genome-resolved taxonomy, global distribution, and EPS potential of Zoogloea, the canonical floc-former in wastewater treatment systems.
items.ab: The bacterial genus Zoogloea is the fourth most abundant genus in wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) globally, where it plays key roles in floc formation and nutrient removal but can also contribute to viscous bulking when highly abundant. The taxonomic assignment of Zoogloea has historically been inconsistent, as several taxa were classified based on phenotypic characteristics and later reassigned to other families or orders. This has obscured both the identity and distribution of Zoogloea and hindered interpretation of its floc-forming mechanisms, which have been attributed to polysaccharides that may not originate from phylogenetically defined Zoogloea. Using our collection of more than 22,000 high-quality genomes from global activated sludge systems (MiDAS global genome catalog), we identified 47 genomes affiliated with the phylogenetically defined Zoogloea. In combination with abundance data, this enabled resolution of the genus' taxonomy, biogeographical distribution, and metabolic diversity. Building on this framework, we mapped the phylogenetic distribution of a recently identified Zoogloea-associated floc-forming polysaccharide biosynthesis gene cluster by screening the MiDAS global genome catalog and GTDB. items.t: Phylogenomic and Comparative Genomic Analyses Support the Monophyly and Genomic Cohesion of the Pseudomonas Fluorescens Lineage but Not the Broader “Pseudomonas_E” Grouping
items.ab: The genus Pseudomonas comprises a large and diverse group of bacteria of major clinical, ecological, and biotechnological importance. Genome-based studies have shown that species currently assigned to this genus are distributed among multiple distinct evolutionary lineages. In this study, we examined the evolutionary relationships and genomic cohesion of the Fluorescens lineage using genome sequences from more than 450 members of the family Pseudomonadaceae. Phylogenomic trees constructed from multiple datasets, including 987 core proteins, the Bac120 marker set, a six-protein housekeeping dataset, and 16S rRNA gene sequences, consistently recovered the Fluorescens lineage as a large and strongly supported monophyletic clade. Whole-genome similarity analyses based on average amino acid identity, percentage of conserved proteins, and Dice similarity further supported the genomic cohesion of this lineage. Pangenome analyses identified 18 protein families for which homologs sharing a minimum of 50% sequence identity and 50% sequence length were present in all examined members of the Fluorescens lineage but absent from other species in the analyzed dataset. items.t: Taxonomic and genomic characterization of 18 novel Deinococcus species isolated from Antarctica.
items.ab: Deinococcus is a genus of bacteria widely known for their resistance to multiple stresses, including ionizing radiation, desiccation and oxidative stress. These extremophiles have been isolated from various environments, including hydrothermal vents, deserts, alpine and polar soils, radioactive sites, car air-conditioning systems and aquatic ecosystems. This study aimed to explore genomic properties of novel Deinococcus species isolated from Antarctica for their putative roles in the carbon and nitrogen cycles, environmental stress resistance and bioremediation. We discovered 18 novel species, which were shown to resist UV radiation and possess multiple genes involved in DNA repair systems for UV-induced damages. Their genomes also contain genes involved in the resistance against other environmental stresses, including extreme cold, heat shock, desiccation, oxidative stress, nutrient depletion, anaerobiosis, halogenated compounds and heavy metals. All studied strains possess the genes for anaplerotic carbon fixation and carbonic anhydrase for the uptake of CO2, enabling them to replenish tricarboxylic acid intermediates. items.t: Functional genomic analysis of Vreelandella zhaodongensis BS253: a new isolate from hypersaline lakes from Brazilian Pantanal.
items.ab: Natural ecosystems harbor an immense diversity of microorganisms whose metabolic capabilities remain unexplored. Therefore, the investigation of microbial life in diverse environments can reveal bacteria with unique physiological and biochemical traits, which may be useful for biotechnological applications. In this study, we report the complete genome sequencing and functional characterization of isolate BS253, isolated in a hypersaline alkaline lake from Brazil's Pantanal region. Using a hybrid sequencing strategy combining Oxford Nanopore long reads and Illumina short reads, we assembled a circular chromosome of 3.76 Mb and two plasmids. Phylogenetic and comparative genomic analyses identified the isolate as Vreelandella zhaodongensis. Digital DNA-DNA hybridization (76.4%) and ANI (96.83%) values supported the designation of BS253 as a strain of V. zhaodongensis. Genome mining revealed genes potentially associated with salt and alkali tolerance, hydrocarbon and plastic degradation, and the biosynthesis of secondary metabolites. Phenotypically, BS253 is a moderately halophilic, facultatively anaerobic, Gram-negative rod that also exhibits emulsifying activity (55.1%) under defined culture conditions. These findings highlight strain BS253 as a metabolically versatile extremophile and a promising candidate for future studies in environmental and industrial biotechnology.

items.t: Leaching Potential and Environmental Implications of Gold Ore Tailings From Ileki Ijesha, Osun State, Nigeria
items.ab: Abstract Gold mining in Nigeria, particularly artisanal and small-scale operations, generates large volumes of tailings that pose serious environmental and public health risks due to heavy metal leaching and potential acid mine drainage (AMD). This study assessed the leaching behavior and geochemical characteristics of gold ore tailings from Ileki Ijesha, Osun State, using batch and dynamic column leaching experiments. Five representative samples were analyzed for pH and concentrations of key metals (Fe, Mn, Pb, Cd, Zn, Cr, Ca) by Atomic Absorption Spectrometry. Leachates were further evaluated through PHREEQC geochemical modeling for speciation, saturation indices, and sensitivity analysis. Results revealed elevated iron (up to 22.2 mg/L) and manganese (up to 11.2 mg/L) concentrations, with moderate lead levels (6.6–7.81 mg/L) under near-neutral pH conditions (6.06–7.73). Modeling indicated supersaturation with iron (oxy) hydroxides and a critical pH threshold (~ 5.5) for accelerated metal release. These findings highlight significant long-term AMD risks and underscore the urgent need for improved tailings management and regulatory frameworks in Nigerian gold mining regions.

items.t: Genomic and experimental evidence from Antarctic geothermal sites indicates diverse thermophiles are globally cosmopolitan
items.ab: Abstract Mt. Erebus, the world’s southernmost active volcano, is highly isolated, yet a previous study found its heated soils contain prokaryotes found elsewhere globally. This was unexpected, as non-sporulating thermophilic microorganisms are thought to be dispersal limited. We searched for the presence of metagenome assembled genomes (MAGs) from Antarctic geothermal sites outside Antarctica, finding that 62% of MAGs had matching species globally. Three of these cosmopolitan thermophiles isolated from Mt. Erebus could survive atmospheric-like conditions, with UV being the strongest selective pressure. Moreover, hot soils from Hawaiʻi sampled four years after a lava flow hosted many thermophilic MAGs with identical strains elsewhere globally, indicating that dispersal/recolonisation by thermophiles can be rapid. Finally, ice core sections from Fang Glacier (Mt. Erebus) associated with volcanic events were enriched in thermophiles, implying that thermophiles could disperse via volcanic events. Our findings dispel the common conception of thermophilic microorganisms as being inherently dispersal limited.

items.t: Discrepant responses of abundant and rare taxa to polyethylene microplastic and nanoplastic perturbations in cold seep sediment.
items.ab: Microplastics (MPs) and nanoplastics (NPs) are emerging contaminants in deep-sea ecosystems, yet their specific impacts on the internal heterogeneity of cold seep microbiomes remain poorly understood. Here, microcosm experiments with cold seep sediments exposed to polyethylene particles were conducted to investigate the response patterns of abundant and rare taxa to MP/NP-induced disturbances. The results indicated that MPs/NPs exposure reshaped bacterial community structure, with significant enrichment of Epsilonbacteraeota, a phylum associated with chemoautotrophic metabolism. In contrast, archaeal alpha diversity showed no significant response to MPs/NPs exposure. Abundant and rare taxa exhibited contrasting responses in community composition, assembly patterns, and network associations. Despite stochastic processes largely governing overall community assembly, the assembly mechanism of rare bacteria shifted toward heterogeneous selection under NPs exposure, which contrasted sharply with the homogeneous selection observed in the rare archaea. Furthermore, network analysis revealed that rare taxa constituted the majority of nodes in both co-occurrence networks. Functional predictions suggested contrasting responses, with lower relative abundances of taxa assigned to sulfate respiration in abundant bacteria under most treatments and higher relative abundances of taxa assigned to sulfur oxidation and nitrogen cycling in rare taxa under some treatments. items.t: Evolutionary histories of microbial calcification-associated genes across the tree of life.
items.ab: UNLABELLED: Biocalcification, a widespread process by which animals and algae form hard tissues and cellular structures, has played a major role in the global carbon cycle over the past 541 Ma. Extracellular or intracellular carbonates are formed by diverse bacteria, yet the genetic basis and evolutionary history of this process remain poorly resolved. Here, we present a large-scale survey of an intracellular calcification marker (calcyanin) and two calcification-associated genes with potential mineralization-promoting roles (carbonic anhydrase [CA] and urease) across the Bacteria and Archaea domains. High-sequence-coverage homologs of calcyanin are restricted to oxygenic cyanobacteria and consistent with vertical inheritance within seven families, suggesting a possible origin in a common ancestor of the Cyanobacteriia class, although some cases likely reflect horizontal gene transfer (HGT). In contrast, CA genes are widespread across all domains of life, with phylogenetic and structural analyses supporting independent origins of the α-, β-, and γ-classes, followed by extensive inter-phylum and possible inter-domain HGT events. items.t: Multi-layer analysis of gut metagenomic functional potential in major depressive disorder.
items.ab: BACKGROUND: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is associated with gut microbiota dysbiosis, but previous studies have mostly focused on species composition and are subject to confounding factors such as age and diet. Robust differences at the functional pathway level remain unclear. items.t: Metagenomic insights into microplastic micro-interfaces: Transforming pollutants and spreading resistance.
items.ab: Microplastic micro-interfaces (MPMI) in wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) serve as critical hubs for microbial colonization, pollutant transformation, and antibiotic resistance gene (ARG) dissemination. In this study, a large-scale genome-resolved metagenomic approach was employed to reconstruct 463 quality-filtered metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) from biofilms established on polyethylene terephthalate (PET), polyethylene (PE), and polypropylene (PP) within a municipal WWTP. Functionally, the MPMI microbiome constructed a highly integrated metabolic network. Dominant lineages were found to synergistically couple aromatic hydrocarbon degradation (via the shikimate pathway and β-oxidation) with complex carbon, nitrogen, and sulfur cycling, while deploying energy-efficient nucleotide salvage strategies to ensure biofilm stabilization under nutrient stress. Crucially, horizontal gene transfer (HGT) emerged as a fundamental mechanism for functional diversification, facilitating the active cross-genomic exchange of key adaptive traits associated with pollutant metabolism and biofilm regulation. items.t: Reducing acid mine drainage potential in sulfide-rich tailings through selective sulfide removal: A case study from a polymetallic mine deposit in northeastern Türkiye
items.ab: Abstract Sulfide-rich mine tailings represent a major source of acid mine drainage (AMD) and associated metal mobilization. This study evaluates selective pyrite flotation as a source-control strategy for reducing the acid-generation potential of flotation tailings from a polymetallic Pb-Zn mine. items.ab: Aerobic composting offers a sustainable route for recycling aquaculture-derived particulates, but appropriate moisture conditions for these fine and adhesive materials remain unclear because conventional criteria are mainly derived from terrestrial wastes. items.t: Seasonal and evolutionary patterns of planktonic Hikarchaeia reveal ecological niches of marine rare biosphere constituents.
items.ab: Members of Marine Group IV, now termed Hikarchaeia, hold an important transitional evolutionary position among Archaea but remain uncultivated, and their ecology remains uncharacterized. items.t: A phyllosphere bacterium Exiguobacterium aurantiacum S11 mitigates cadmium toxicity in seagrass (Zostera marina) via a synergistic "exclusion-redox-repair" network.
items.ab: Heavy metal pollution, particularly cadmium (Cd), threatens coastal marine ecosystems and foundational species like the seagrass Zostera marina. Here, a multi-extremophilic phyllosphere bacterium, Exiguobacterium aurantiacum S11, was isolated to investigate its capacity and multi-dimensional molecular networks in mitigating acute Cd toxicity in Z. marina. In vitro assays confirmed high Cd tolerance in strain S11, driven by cell-surface biosorption and genomic active efflux systems (czcD, cadD, zupT, and znuA) regulated by cadC and resD. In an 18-day mesocosm challenge model utilizing 500 μM Cd, S11 inoculation reduced root Cd accumulation by 38.3% (p < 0.05) and attenuated systemic oxidative stress by suppressing malondialdehyde and stabilizing glutathione peroxidase activity. Furthermore, S11 specifically activated host folate biosynthesis, vitamin B6 metabolism, and DNA Base Excision Repair (BER) pathways, while promoting the accumulation of defensive diterpenes, flavonoids, and isoflavonoids. Overall, E. aurantiacum S11 establishes a synergistic "exclusion-redox-repair" network that enhances host resilience, offering a novel microbially assisted strategy for marine ecological restoration.

items.t: Sulphate removal from synthetic acid mine drainage by iron-impregnated coconut shell biochar: role of iron retention and surface accessibility
items.ab: Abstract Acid mine drainage (AMD) carries high sulphate loads that lime neutralisation removes poorly. Iron-modified biochars are promising anion adsorbents, but the roles of iron loading and iron accessibility are rarely separated. In this study, coconut shell biochar produced at 650°C was impregnated with FeCl 3 ·6H 2 O at precursor-to-biochar mass ratios of 0.5, 0.7 and 1.0 g g − 1 (FeBC-0.5, FeBC-0.7 and FeBC-1.0). items.ab: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is associated with changes in gut microbiota composition and predicted microbial functions that may relate to intestinal immune processes. This study compared gut microbiota profiles between individuals with IBD and healthy controls and examined predicted microbial pathways and their associations with bacterial genera. Publicly available 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing data from 22 stool samples (11 IBD and 11 healthy controls) were analysed. Taxonomic profiling, diversity analysis, differential abundance testing, and PICRUSt2-based functional prediction were performed. items.ab: Streptomyces griseorubens strain MEPSL1 is an endophytic actinomycetes isolated from sweet potato roots, with its 16S rRNA gene and genome sequence previously deposited in the NCBI database. items.t: Multilayer defense collapse model and rare taxa-based early warning for solid-state vinegar fermentation stagnation: A time-series metagenomic study.
items.ab: Fermentation stagnation is a persistent challenge in industrial vinegar production, yet its microecological mechanisms remain poorly understood. We found fermentation stagnation represents a cascade collapse of four progressive defense layers rather than a single-point failure. The acidic chemical barrier subsequently fails through both barrier weakening and quorum sensing-mediated active breakthrough. Antimicrobial peptide defense ultimately collapses with 74% AMP decline, driving the system into a dysregulated steady state characterized by broad-spectrum resistome expansion. items.t: Ecological partitioning and functional specialization of Thermoproteota across multiple trench sediments.
items.ab: Thermoproteota (formerly referred to as Thaumarchaeota) are phylogenetically divided into ammonia-oxidizing archaea (AOA) affiliated with Nitrososphaeria and basal non-ammonia-oxidizing archaea (non-AOA). items.t: Enhanced remediation of wastewater impacted by acid mine drainage at low temperature using sulfate-reducing bacteria immobilized in biomass-amended PVA-SA beads.
items.ab: Acid mine drainage (AMD) is a severe environmental threat owing to its high acidity, sulfate, and heavy metal content with devastating effects on watershed ecosystems. items.t: Cross-domain microbiome legacy of a natural Phaeocystis globosa bloom in eutrophic coastal waters: a framework for monitoring bloom onset, collapse, and post-bloom recovery.
items.ab: When a harmful algal bloom collapses, does the coastal water quality recover? items.t: Chromosome-level genome assembly and annotation of the parthenogenetic nematode Acrobeloides nanus
items.ab: Acrobeloides nanus is a species of widely distributed bacteria-feeding nematodes belonging to the family Cephalobidae. It reproduces parthenogenetically, making it a valuable system for studying the consequences of obligate asexuality, and exhibits early developmental processes that differ significantly from the model organism Caenorhabditis elegans. Additionally, the species has demonstrated remarkable resistance in extreme conditions, surviving near-complete desiccation through anhydrobiosis. This new chromosome-level genome assembly provides a high-quality reference to study these traits. Combining Nanopore, amplified PacBio HiFi, and Hi-C sequencing, we generated a chromosome-level assembly spanning 188.9 Mb over six chromosomes. The genome features a 48.1% repeat content, dominated by Mutator-like elements, and contains 24,912 predicted genes. Structural analysis reveals the conservation of ancestral nematode linkage groups. This resource significantly improves upon previous fragmented assemblies, offering a new framework for identifying genomic adaptations in the family Cephalobidae.

items.ab: Host-associated prokaryotes can undergo extreme genome reduction, but the most reduced genomes belong to mutualistic endosymbionts whose hosts compensate for lost functions, eroding the symbiont's identity as an autonomous cell. items.ab: Protists are vastly diverse, forming over 20 supergroups of the eukaryotic diversity and fulfilling plentiful functions. Rhizaria is a widespread and highly abundant clade comprising important parasites and a huge diversity of free-living heterotrophic predators. items.t: Comparative performance of reference-based metagenomic tools to identify species-level taxa among families of bacteria: benchmarking Mycobacteriaceae and Neisseriaceae.
items.ab: UNLABELLED: Hypotheses concerning the ecology and evolution of bacteria commonly relate to the presence and abundance of species in various settings and conditions. Shotgun metagenomics may address these hypotheses, which previously relied on PCR or culture. However, the problem of determining the presence/absence of a given species of interest is not trivial, particularly when closely related species are present in the reference database or metagenomic sample. Reference-based methods for detecting species-level taxa mostly rely on thresholding of aligned reads or mapped k-mers, or derivative metrics such as genomic coverage, creating a trade-off between recall/completeness and precision/purity. New methods for species-level profiling (YACHT, Metapresence, and sylph) have recently been published. Here, we test the performance of these methods, along with Kraken2/bracken and MetaPhlAn4, to detect related species of interest using simulated metagenomic samples from genomes in the families Mycobacteriaceae and Neisseriaceae, which contain closely related genomes. Among methods tested, Metapresence, when used with an alignment quality filter, and sylph offer the best overall performance. Sylph maintains high precision but requires a depth of coverage greater than approximately 0.1× to reliably detect a genome's presence. items.t: Deep-sea siliceous sponges harbor distinct and functionally diverse microbiomes.
items.ab: Sponges, phylum Porifera, are long-lived and basal-branching metazoans that play important roles in ocean biogeochemistry and host diverse microbial communities. Siliceous sponges form a major clade of the Porifera; however, their microbiome is not well characterized, particularly in the deep ocean. Here, we used shotgun metagenomics to investigate the composition of the microbial communities of 13 siliceous sponges collected from four sites near Puerto Rico from depths ranging from 400 to 1,900 meters. Nine of the sponges in this study are from five sponge families that have not previously been sequenced using shotgun metagenomics. We assembled a total of 176 metagenome-assembled genomes from 20 bacterial phyla and 1 archaeal phylum. Ammonia-oxidizing archaea (AOA) Nitrosopumilaceae dominated most siliceous sponge microbial communities and was strikingly the sole symbiont associated with one sponge (Farrea). Overall, microbiome diversity was relatively low across siliceous sponges, except for a Phloeodictyidae, which is likely a high microbial abundance (HMA) sponge. Our results suggest that host sponge phylogeny may shape microbial community structure, with limited evidence for an environmental role. The sponge-associated microbial communities contained genetic capabilities for diverse metabolic functions, particularly contributing to the carbon, nitrogen, and sulfur cycles. items.t: Integrating bacteriophage-mediated gene mobility into microbiological risk assessment: A framework for food safety.
items.ab: Bacteriophages occupy a structurally contradictory position in modern food systems. Since 2006 they have been approved in multiple jurisdictions as biocontrol agents applied directly to food, and are now routinely deployed against Listeria monocytogenes, Escherichia coli O157:H7 and Salmonella enterica. In parallel, phages are the principal vehicles of transduction, the horizontal transfer mechanism by which antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs) and virulence determinants move between bacterial cells. Current microbiological risk assessment (MRA) frameworks resolve this asymmetrically: phage biocontrol enters quantitative models as a log-reduction term, whereas phage-mediated gene mobility is rarely represented explicitly. Current evidence suggests that this pathway now warrants explicit consideration. The discovery of lateral transduction, which mobilises chromosomal regions at frequencies orders of magnitude above classical generalised transduction, indicates that phage-mediated transfer is, in the systems where it has been measured, not a rare packaging error but a routine feature of temperate phage life cycles, although its prevalence, rates, host range and ecological importance across food-associated communities remain insufficiently resolved. Concurrently, viromics, whole-genome sequencing, proximity ligation and emerging transductomic approaches have made the food-chain phageome quantifiable for the first time. items.t: Thermophilization but weak phosphorus-affinity shifts in freshwater phytoplankton communities
items.ab: Climate warming and nutrient enrichment are reshaping many freshwater lakes, yet their relative roles in driving directional changes in phytoplankton communities across broad geographic gradients remain poorly understood. Using data from lakes repeatedly surveyed by the U.S. National Lakes Assessment in 2012, 2017, and 2022, we examined whether warming and phosphorus enrichment produced comparable shifts in phytoplankton community composition, environmental affinities, and cell size structure. Temporal compositional change increased with the magnitude of temperature change but was not significantly associated with changes in phosphorus concentration. Communities showed thermophilization, shifting toward taxa associated with warmer conditions as temperature increased, primarily through gains of warmer-affinity taxa. In contrast, phosphorus-affinity shifts were not significantly related to phosphorus change. Average community-level phytoplankton cell size declined with warming but did not respond to phosphorus change. These results suggest that temperature change drive more consistent taxonomic and functional reorganization than phosphorus change in freshwater phytoplankton communities.

items.t: Multi-response Optimization of Acidithiobacillus ferrooxidans Cultivation for Enhanced Biomass Growth and Soluble Ferric Iron Production
items.ab: Abstract Optimizing the growth of Acidithiobacillus ferrooxidans is essential for enhancing its efficiency in bioleaching and biomining applications. In this study, response surface methodology based on a central composite design was applied to evaluate the individual and interactive effects of pH, inoculum density, and ferrous sulphate concentration on growth kinetics and redox performance. Ferrous iron concentration and inoculum density were identified as the most influential factors, significantly affecting biomass production, specific growth rate, and ferric iron accumulation, whereas pH exerted a comparatively smaller effect within the investigated range. Significant interaction effects among the cultivation variables were observed, demonstrating the importance of considering factor interactions during process optimization. Multi-response optimization predicted that cultivation at pH 1.8, 10% inoculum, and 45 g/L FeSO₄ would support a specific growth rate of 0.053 h − 1 while maintaining elevated soluble ferric iron concentrations (8.497 g/L) within the tested range. Under these conditions, ferric iron remained comparatively stable in solution, indicating reduced ferric loss through precipitation. These findings highlight inoculum density as an important yet often overlooked cultivation parameter and demonstrate the value of statistically guided bioprocess optimization for improving A. ferrooxidans cultivation and ferric iron availability for bioleaching applications.

items.t: VARIANT: Web server for decoding and analyzing viral mutations at genome and protein levels.
items.ab: A comprehensive analysis of viral mutations is essential for understanding viral evolution, disease epidemiology, diagnosis, drug resistance, and immune escape. However, challenges remain in capturing complex mutation patterns and supporting diverse viral families with varying genome architectures. To address these challenges, we present VARIANT, an openly accessible web server for mutational analysis of RNA viral genomes and associated viral products across both single- and multi-segment virus genomes. The server takes a viral reference genome, a reference protein sequence, and/or a multiple sequence alignment as inputs, and automatically provides full annotation of mutation types, including standard categories such as point mutations (missense, silent, and nonsense), insertions, deletions, and frameshift events in both coding and noncoding regions. In addition, VARIANT detects two biologically significant mutation patterns that are often overlooked by conventional software/packages, including "row mutations" and "hot mutations," and separately annotates potential programmed ribosomal frameshifting regions. The server currently contains automatic analysis of major viral pathogens, including SARS-CoV-2, HIV-1, influenza H3N2, Ebola virus, and Chikungunya virus. It also allows users to analyze additional viruses by uploading custom genome information. Users can track VARIANT analysis progress in real time, visualize mutation distributions, and download structured results in ZI

items.ab: Abstract The Kryptonia are a candidate bacterial phylum of extreme thermophiles from terrestrial hot springs with reduced genomes and obligate fermentative metabolism. items.t: Oxygen availability shapes microbial community composition and function to determine antibiotic resistance genes and expression during composting: A pilot-scale study.
items.ab: Temperature was considered the primary factor reducing antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) during composting, with oxygen availability serving as the fundamental driver of temperature differences. However, how different oxygen levels shaped the composition and function of microbial communities, and subsequently affected ARGs and resistance expression during composting, remained unclear. Here, a pilot-scale long-term thermophilic aerobic and mesophilic facultative composting were constructed with metagenomics and stress (Oxygen/Antibiotic) plate screening to reveal the resistance potential and direct risk. The ratios of aerobic, facultative, and anaerobic bacteria were 1:0.94:0.75 in aerobic composting, and 1:0.96:0.99 in facultative composting. Metabolic functions were significantly enriched in aerobic composting, promoting temperature rise (peak 54 °C). In facultative composting, functions related to horizontal gene transfer and transcription/translation were enriched. Compared with mesophilic facultative composting, aerobic composting significantly reduced ARGs abundance (from 4.80 to 3.59 CPC) and mobility (from 3.66 to 2.27 CPC). ARGs hosts in aerobic composting were widely distributed, predominantly among aerobic microorganisms, while ARGs hosts in facultative composting were more concentrated, mostly among facultative anaerobes. items.t: Uncovering novel phage defense systems through genomic island analysis in Streptococcus thermophilus
items.ab: Bacteria encode diverse antiviral defense systems, yet the evolutionary reservoirs that generate this immune innovation remain poorly defined. Although genomic context has been instrumental in discovering defense systems, genomic islands (GIs), variable chromosomal regions enriched in defense genes and proteins of unknown function, have not been systematically explored as sources of new bacterial immunity. Here, using comparative genomics of Streptococcus thermophilus, we identified 30 defense-associated GIs displaying extensive accessory gene diversity. Investigation of candidate loci from three GIs uncovered 15 previously uncharacterized antiviral systems, including 10 with novel architectures or features, revealing the potential within even a small subset of GIs. Several systems were not located near known defense genes, highlighting that GI-based discovery complements the traditional guilt-by-association approach, revealing systems that would otherwise remain undetected. Together, our findings establish GIs as reservoirs of antiviral innovation and provide a framework for uncovering the diversity of bacterial immune systems.

items.t: Thermococcales pangenome uncovers new genera and modular evolution
items.ab: The order Thermococcales is unusual among Archaea in being known primarily from hundreds of lab-cultured isolates rather than metagenome-assembled genomes. Such cultivation is powerful for comparative genomics, allowing access to complete closed genomes rather than fragmented assemblies. We analysed 122 complete genomes, comprising all publicly available type species plus 67 new isolates, as a single pangenome. A combination of genome-scale metrics resolved 70 species across five genus-level clades, two proposed here as the new genera Oleococcus and Piezococcus , in addition to the canonical Pyrococcus, Palaeococcus, and Thermococcus. Only 6.1% of the 21,490 gene families are persistent, yet these contribute over half the genes in any genome. We observe that accessory functions, such as amino-acid biosynthesis, often behave modularly, being gained and lost as intact cassettes from genus-specific chromosomal loci. Combined with 114 mobile genetic elements, 72 integrated into the chromosome at conserved tRNA genes, and 42 extrachromosomal, we find that Thermococcales genomes accommodate rapid horizontal turnover through a constrained chromosomal architecture.

items.t: Pangenome-resolved deconvolution of gut metatranscriptomes reveals species-specific microbial activity programs in Parkinson’s disease
items.ab: Abstract Gut microbiome alterations are associated with Parkinson’s disease (PD), yet their species-level functional consequences remain poorly understood. Here, we develop a pangenome-resolved framework integrating paired metagenomic and metatranscriptomic data to reconstruct species-level transcriptional profiles. Applied to two independent cohorts comprising 160 individuals and 7,548 profiles across 215 species, this approach revealed reduced genome-wide transcriptional breadth and increased inter-individual heterogeneity in PD. Genomic diversity and transcriptomic variation were significantly associated in 61 of 95 tested species. We identified 2,271 pangenome-resolved features associated with disease status, duration, or severity, with 39% of significant gene-level associations involving accessory genes. Species-specific responses included reduced metabolic and biosynthetic expression in commensals, including Coprococcus aceti and Streptococcus thermophilus, alongside increased stress-adaptation, mucin-degradation, and metal-homeostasis functions in other taxa. Cross-cohort classification performance varied substantially between species. These findings establish pangenome-resolved metatranscriptomics as a framework for identifying lineage-specific functional responses within microbiomes.

items.t: Microbiologically influenced corrosion in extreme environments caused by problematic microbial biofilms.
items.ab: Microbiologically influenced corrosion (MIC) caused by microbial biofilms poses significant challenges to industrial systems. MIC and MIC mitigation cost billions of dollars each year in the US alone. Although most microbes flourish under mild conditions, increasing evidence demonstrates that in extreme environments such as high temperature, pressure, salinity, and low pH, extremophiles including thermophiles, barophiles, halophiles, and acidophiles can still form resilient biofilms and contribute to corrosion and biofouling. This review summarizes recent advances in understanding the formation, adaptation, and persistence of microbial biofilms in extreme environments and their roles in MIC. Key corrosion mechanisms such as extracellular electron transfer-MIC (EET-MIC) and metabolite-MIC (M-MIC) are discussed with environmental stressors and microbial physiology. Existing studies reveal that extreme environmental conditions do not necessarily suppress MIC, as extremophiles can adapt to environmental stresses and maintain corrosive activities. Different environmental stressors affect MIC through various pathways such as microbial metabolism and corrosion kinetics. Representative case studies highlight MIC behaviors under deep-sea, geothermal, hypersaline, and acidic conditions that are relevant to industrial operations. items.t: Williamsia profundi sp. nov., a novel deep-sea Actinomycetota isolate with versatile metabolic potential and specialized ecological adaptability.
items.ab: The deep-sea biosphere hosts distinctive microbial communities with specialized adaptive traits, yet the mechanisms underpinning their physiological survival remain largely obscure.
